title: node-forge 1.4.3 corrections: certificate, Ed25519 and TLS/HTTP applicability
summary: Signed prerelease 27.3.0-beta.5 ships node-forge 1.4.3 in Server/PKI after successful Windows release validation. It corrects additional upstream certificate nameConstraints, Ed25519 small-order-key and Forge TLS/HTTP findings. Reviewed 27.2.5 and 27.3.0-beta.4 lockfiles include 1.4.2. A remotely exploitable Vision One path has not been established. Resolution identifies a published patched prerelease, not a stable-channel patch or a recommendation to deploy beta software without acceptance.

affected.product: Vision One Server / packaged Windows Runtime and separately maintained PKI tooling
affected.versions: Reviewed 27.2.5 and 27.3.0-beta.4 include node-forge 1.4.2, within the upstream affected dependency range. This is dependency inclusion, not demonstrated product exploitability. Earlier releases, customer integrations and dynamic third-party paths have not been comprehensively assessed and must not be assumed unaffected.
affected.action: For environments approved for prerelease use, evaluate the signed beta-5 installer with backups and site acceptance. Stable 27.2.5 is not a fix for these additional findings; stable-only installations should request a supported remediation plan. Do not manually replace packaged libraries. Separately deployed PKI tooling requires its own controlled update.

impact: Upstream rates the nameConstraints chain-verification finding High, Forge TLS/HTTP denial-of-service findings Moderate and Ed25519 small-order-key verification Low (CVE-2026-125335). Impacts concern certificate-chain acceptance outside permitted names, forged-signature acceptance for small-order keys, TLS client crashes and HTTP parsing CPU exhaustion in the corresponding Forge APIs. These are upstream impacts and ratings, not demonstrated Vision One attacks or a product-specific CVSS score. No license, authentication or runtime TLS bypass has been demonstrated by this review.

The workflow-created source tag identifies f587c5d9d0c75ca16b852efcdadab06bd5d85877. This is not a penetration test or stable 27.3 sign-off.

Fresh release-preparation npm audits initially aggregated four advisories into one moderate node-forge package entry in each of Server and PKI: GHSA-6889-vf6x-f3g5, GHSA-w4xr-hqv8-ch44, GHSA-6cv4-p8m7-4r25 and GHSA-j8rw-jp99-435v. Updating both to 1.4.3 cleared those entries. The upstream changelog additionally lists High GHSA-3cc4-3294-vgjf (nameConstraints), absent from that initial npm output; npm metadata alone is therefore not the basis of this assessment.

The bounded application-source review found Forge used for RSA/CSR/certificate generation, parsing and metadata inspection, not production Forge Ed25519, TLS/HTTP clients or verifyCertificateChain calls. License verification uses Node crypto Ed25519; HTTPS and Project Replication use Node TLS/crypto. PKI regression fixtures exercise Forge chain verification. This does not establish universal non-exploitability or cover every dynamic dependency/customer integration.

Added regressions reject a small-order Ed25519 public key. Existing tests cover plain/encrypted CA keys, CSR validation, native/Forge chain verification, certificate metadata and retained key material. No malicious network payload or customer-plant test was performed. Replacing the dependency does not renew certificates, repair previously accepted external data or update a running process without restart.

This notice covers the additional 1.4.3 findings, separately from the older RSA CVE in VO-SA-2026-001. The previously published 1.4.2 RSA correction remains valid for that distinct issue. A beta fix must not be misread as a stable 27.2 patch; stable-only operators still require coordinated supported remediation.
remediation: Use the signed 27.3.0-beta.5 installer only where prerelease deployment is approved, after full backups and installation-specific acceptance. Stable-only installations should request a supported remediation plan; 27.2.5 retains the affected dependency for these new findings. Do not replace individual packaged modules or disable certificate checks. Update separately deployed PKI tooling through its supported maintenance process, retain existing private material and review any required certificate/fingerprint trust changes. Restart updated services under the maintenance procedure.
workarounds: Keep runtime, replication and maintenance endpoints within approved OT segments or VPNs and restrict filesystem access to certificate/key/CSR material. These measures reduce exposure but do not patch the library or establish a complete workaround.

Accept external PKI material only from approved sources; retain TLS hostname, chain and peer-fingerprint verification. Inventory custom integrations that invoke Forge Ed25519, TLS, HTTP or certificate-chain verification and request an installation-specific assessment.

Keep build/maintenance tooling isolated from untrusted network access and inputs. Do not use a clean npm audit or the absence of a demonstrated product exploit as proof that every runtime path is safe.

title: Node2Shell: Brotli runtime applicability and external Node.js updates
summary: Vision One 27.2.5 adds a pre-start Node safety gate for externally started servers and retains the corrected Electron 44.10.1 embedded decoder already reviewed in 27.2.4. The finding is resolved for the reviewed updated deployment paths. Older installations and external Node executables still require update and restart; publication of this notice does not patch a running process or establish every older installer's applicability.

affected.product: Vision One server started with an external Node.js executable
affected.versions: The 27.2.4 HTTP parsing path was reviewed. Exposure depends on the actual runtime binary and network reachability, not just the Vision One version. Upstream fixed releases are Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 in their respective lines. Older installers and other deployment combinations remain outside this bounded review and must not be assumed unaffected.
fixedVersions: 27.2.5 (startup safety gate; actual Node executable must meet the floor)
27.3.0-rc.1 (published signed release candidate; same startup floor)
27.3.0-rc.2 (published signed release candidate; standalone Node >=26.13.1 or separately checked embedded Electron runtime)
affected.action: Update to a supported release and use its supported server entrypoint. Through RC 1 the startup policy permits Node 24.x >=24.22.1 or Node >=26.12.1 with newer-line warnings. RC 2 requires stable standalone Node 26.x >=26.13.1; newer major lines and above-floor prereleases warn, while standalone Node 24 is blocked because of a separate WASM/V8 crash. Embedded Node 24 requires separately checked Electron/Chromium V8 floors. Update the actual service executable and restart; the installer cannot update a separately managed Node binary. Permission to start is not ongoing native compatibility or security qualification.

affected.versions: Published signed 27.2.4 and 27.2.5 ship Electron 44.10.1 with Node 24.22.1 and Chromium 152.0.7977.169. The reviewed embedded Brotli decoder contains the correction. No complete affected-version range or first fixed installer version is established for earlier installers.
fixedVersions: 27.2.4 (reviewed corrected embedded decoder; not an established first fixed version)
27.3.0-beta.4 (published signed prerelease; same reviewed Electron baseline)
27.3.0-beta.5 (published signed prerelease; same reviewed Electron baseline)
27.3.0-rc.1 (published signed release candidate; same reviewed Electron baseline)
27.3.0-rc.2 (published signed release candidate; same reviewed Electron baseline)
affected.action: Use the published signed 27.2.4 installer or a later supported release. Do not replace embedded Node, Electron or packaged library files manually. Assess any separately started services independently.

impact: Upstream rates CVE-2026-111497 High. Malformed Brotli input can cause an out-of-bounds write, potentially leading to a crash, disclosure of process memory or remote code execution. This is an upstream impact statement, not a demonstrated Vision One exploit or a product-specific CVSS score. No exploit payload was used in this review and no customer compromise is claimed.
assessment: Revision 2026-11-13: published signed 27.3.0-rc.2 passed Windows workflow 43415690895 and downloaded installer checksum/publisher signature verification. Development/build/CI now pin Node 26.13.1 LTS. The standalone startup floor is raised to 26.13.1 and standalone Node 24 is rejected after a separate known WASM wrapper-lifetime failure; this is not a new Brotli vulnerability or remediation. Electron 44.10.1 retains embedded Node 24.22.1 with Chromium V8 15.2; its forked server/solver workers use that engine, which contains the identified WASM correction. Embedded acceptance checks Node, Electron and V8 metadata rather than blindly exempting Electron. Bounded repeat checks passed on both actual runtimes. Original stable Brotli recommendations, external executable update/restart requirements and older-installer limits remain.

Revision 2026-11-12: published signed 27.3.0-rc.1 passed authoritative Windows workflow 43232209650 with the same Electron 44.10.1 and external Node startup-floor baselines. This is not a new Brotli fix or blanket qualification of external executables. Original stable recommendations, restart requirements and older-installer scope limitations remain.

Revision 2026-11-11: published signed 27.3.0-beta.5 passed Windows workflow 42992655669 and retains the reviewed Electron 44.10.1 baseline and external Node startup floor. Downloaded installer checksum and valid publisher signature were verified. Existing stable update recommendations, external-runtime restart obligations and older-installer review limitations remain unchanged; this is not a new Brotli fix.

Revision 2026-11-10: signed 27.3.0-beta.4 is published after successful authoritative Windows workflow 42787248122. It retains the standalone startup floor and reviewed Electron 44.10.1 baseline. Downloaded installer SHA-256 and valid publisher Authenticode signature were verified. This prerelease does not supersede stable deployment recommendations or qualify arbitrary external Node executables; update/restart and native-binary review limitations remain.

Release revision 27.2.5 (2026-11-05): the supported server entrypoint checks the actual Node executable before importing runtime code, opening network listeners or starting migrations. It permits Node 24.x >=24.22.1 normally, and all versions >=26.12.1 with a compatibility warning. Other versions are blocked. Startup tests cover rejected versions, safe floors, later prereleases and rejection before runtime import. Electron's reviewed Node 24.22.1 passes the same floor without an exemption. Resolution describes these updated deployment paths; it does not declare older installations patched or every permitted future Node version free of security defects.

The reviewed Express JSON and URL-encoded body parsers accept compressed input. Content-Encoding: br reaches node:zlib Brotli decompression in body-parser before many route-specific authorization checks. Authentication alone must therefore not be treated as a complete mitigation for a reachable unpatched server.

The packaged server is forked through Electron's runtime, not the system-wide node.exe. Electron 44.10.1 reports Node 24.22.1 and Chromium 152.0.7977.169. Electron uses Chromium's Brotli dependency, so the Node version alone was not used as proof: the matching Chromium decoder source rejects max_block_type <= 1 with BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH. A benign local runtime check confirmed that error constant is -17. This is source/runtime corroboration, not an independent exploit test or comprehensive inspection of every installer.

A Brotli version string of 1.2.0 alone does not establish vulnerability because the correction can be backported without changing that string. npm audit assesses npm dependency metadata, not this native decoder in a Node/Electron executable.

Historical initial publication on 2026-11-05 remained open for externally managed Node deployments and the unassessed older-installer scope. The 27.2.5 revision supersedes that product remediation status, not the older-installer review limitations. Updating an executable does not patch already running processes; service and development processes require a controlled restart.

Published 27.2.4 CI used Node 24.15.0 for build tooling. The 27.2.5 release changes the development/CI pin to 24.22.2 and adds a separately evaluated server runtime range. Build/runtime findings remain distinct; no build compromise is asserted.
remediation: Update to the signed Vision One 27.2.5 release or later. For external services, inventory and update the actual Node executable, use the supported main entrypoint and restart the processes; the product update cannot replace a separately managed Node installation. Node 24.22.2 remains the qualified development/CI pin, while the 24.x security floor is 24.22.1 and the newer-line floor is 26.12.1. Newer allowed lines emit a compatibility warning and require installation-specific validation. Do not replace embedded Node/Electron files manually. Retain OT segmentation and request older-installer assessment where necessary.
workarounds: Keep runtime endpoints within approved OT networks, VPNs or equivalent controls. Network restrictions reduce exposure but do not correct an unpatched decoder.

Where an approved reverse proxy is used, rejecting Brotli-encoded request bodies before they reach the server can reduce this path's exposure. Ensure direct backend access is blocked and all ingress paths are covered; this is not a validated complete workaround for every decompression path.

Keep development and build services isolated from untrusted network access and inputs. Do not rely on a clean npm audit, login requirements or a changed version pin as proof that running executables are patched.

title: SMTP certificate verification is disabled by default
summary: Vision One 27.2.5 requires encrypted and certificate-verified SMTP for all outgoing mail, including existing configurations. The disabling UI switch is removed and old configuration flags cannot bypass the transport policy. This resolves the compatibility default described for 27.2.0 through 27.2.4. Mail delivery can stop when a relay lacks TLS or trusted hostname-matching certificates; commissioning and delivery checks remain required. No CVE or CVSS score is assigned.

affected.product: Vision One outbound SMTP mail (alerting, diagnostics and reports)
affected.versions: 27.2.0 through 27.2.4 were reviewed. The default and legacy-settings normalization can disable SMTP certificate verification. Installations with an explicitly enabled and persisted verification choice do not have that disabled-verification configuration, but still require appropriate TLS transport policy. Earlier releases and prereleases are outside this review and must not be assumed unaffected.
affected.action: Update to 27.2.5 or later in an approved maintenance window. Confirm the relay supports STARTTLS or configured implicit TLS and presents a valid hostname-matching chain trusted by the runtime. Verify diagnostic, alarm and report delivery; keep an alternative notification path until accepted.

impact: When SMTP TLS certificate verification is disabled, the runtime accepts a presented mail-server certificate without the normal trust and hostname validation. An attacker able to intercept or redirect the SMTP connection may impersonate the mail server and obtain SMTP credentials or operational email content. This describes the security consequence of the configuration; it is not a claim that an attack or credential compromise has occurred. No CVE is assigned by this notice and no product-specific CVSS score has been established. Severity is therefore displayed as Not rated rather than as an invented numerical or categorical assessment.
assessment: Revision 2026-11-13: published signed 27.3.0-rc.2 passed Windows workflow 43415690895, including mail/runtime checks, and downloaded installer checksum/publisher signature verification. Mandatory SMTP TLS/certificate verification and original stable recommendations remain unchanged. External standalone servers require the RC-2 Node 26.13.1 floor and a controlled restart. Relay trust, hostname coverage and actual alarm/report delivery commissioning remain necessary; this is not plant acceptance.

Revision 2026-11-12: published signed 27.3.0-rc.1 passed authoritative Windows workflow 43232209650, including mail checks, and retains mandatory encrypted/certificate-verified SMTP. Stable remediation is unchanged; relay trust, hostname coverage, controlled restart and delivery commissioning remain necessary. RC publication is not plant acceptance.

Revision 2026-11-11: published signed 27.3.0-beta.5 retains mandatory SMTP TLS/certificate verification and passed the authoritative Windows gate including mail checks. Downloaded installer hash and publisher signature were verified. Relay trust, hostname and delivery commissioning remain required; stable recommendations are unchanged.

Revision 2026-11-10: published signed prerelease 27.3.0-beta.4 retains mandatory SMTP TLS and certificate verification. The authoritative Windows release gate passed, including settings/mail checks; the downloaded installer hash and publisher signature were verified. This adds a reviewed fixed prerelease, not a recommendation to replace a supported stable installation with beta software. Relay trust, hostname and delivery commissioning remain required.

Release revision 27.2.5 (2026-11-05): the central mail transport forces requireTLS=true, ignoreTLS=false, opportunisticTLS=false and tls.rejectUnauthorized=true after loading stored settings and credentials. Certificate verification is normalized as enabled on load and settings API updates. The Mail UI no longer exposes a switch to disable it. Existing implicit TLS remains supported. Tests cover a real local SMTP relay without STARTTLS and an untrusted self-signed TLS endpoint; both fail before SMTP authentication/mail transfer. These are controlled fixtures, not verification of customer relays.

The existing mail.energy-control.it hostname migrates to mail.it-service.bz.it during startup, preserving configured port, sender and credentials. Other hostnames are not replaced but have the same mandatory TLS/certificate policy. New configurations have no embedded password. Settings recovery can still reset configuration and requires review before restoring production notifications.

Historical review through 27.2.4: Nodemailer 10.3.1 was shipped, but the compatibility default and legacy normalization remained. Upgrading to those versions alone did not enforce TLS or enable certificate verification. The 27.2.5 revision supersedes that remediation status; the evidence below records earlier behavior.

The reviewed release source for 27.2.0, 27.2.1 and 27.2.2 sets the SMTP TLS rejectUnauthorized option to false by default. Legacy or imported settings lacking the explicit-choice marker are normalized to false, even if an unmarked legacy verification value was true. Invalid verification values also fall back to false. An upgrade must therefore not be treated as evidence that an earlier verification choice remains active; inspect the effective setting.

Historical behavior through 27.2.4: the supported Mail settings toggle wrote the verification choice and its explicit-choice marker. Earlier tests used isolated configuration and mocked mail transport; they did not validate a customer's relay or constitute a network penetration test. That toggle has been removed in 27.2.5.

Historical transport behavior through 27.2.4: certificate verification alone did not require an encrypted connection or prevent STARTTLS downgrade; secure=false allowed STARTTLS when offered. The 27.2.5 mandatory transport policy replaces this behavior. A successful test email remains only one commissioning check; verify actual TLS and relay requirements with the mail administrator.

This SMTP notice is separate from VO-SA-2026-001 and VO-SA-2026-003. Its resolution does not change HTTPS or Project Replication certificate policy and is not a general claim that all security risks are eliminated.
remediation: Install the signed Vision One 27.2.5 release or later under the site's maintenance procedure. TLS and certificate verification are then mandatory regardless of old stored flags; there is no disable-verification UI switch. Prepare trusted relay certificates, hostname matching and STARTTLS/implicit TLS before the upgrade. Verify delivery with the mail administrator and retain an alternative alarm path until accepted. Correct trust/hostname/relay errors rather than modifying packaged runtime files or disabling certificate checks.
workarounds: Arrange an approved maintenance window and an alternative alarm-notification path before upgrading. Confirm SMTP hostname coverage, certificate validity and runtime trust of the complete chain. Browser trust alone is not sufficient evidence of runtime trust.

For older versions awaiting upgrade, the existing Settings > Mail verification toggle can harden certificate checks when commissioned correctly, but does not itself enforce TLS. This is temporary configuration hardening, not a substitute for the 27.2.5 transport policy. After upgrade, verification is mandatory and the switch is absent.

Use the approved Diagnostic email recipient and Send test email action in Settings > Mail. This recipient is a global technical-diagnostics setting, not a one-off test address; if it is changed temporarily, restore the intended configuration, including an empty value if diagnostics were disabled. Verify receipt and then test required alarm/report workflows under the site procedure.

Have the mail administrator verify actual TLS negotiation, certificate trust and required delivery workflows using appropriate relay/runtime diagnostics. A relay lacking TLS or trusted certificates is intentionally rejected after upgrade.

If certificate validation fails, correct the hostname, certificate or trust configuration before repeating the test. Do not use permanent disabling of verification as the remedy. Keep the alternative notification path active until the required workflows are verified.

Restrict mail-server connectivity and administrative access to approved networks and accounts. These are defense-in-depth controls, not a complete substitute for authenticated, TLS-required mail transport.

title: node-forge RSA signature verification: Vision One applicability assessment
summary: Vision One 27.2.4 ships node-forge 1.4.2, including the upstream correction for CVE-2026-85393 first released in 1.4.1. The dependency finding is resolved in this published product version. Reviewed 27.2.0 through 27.2.3 baselines include node-forge 1.4.0, with the affected verifier reachable through local CSR handling. Remote exploitability in Vision One has not been established. High severity refers to the upstream library advisory, not a separately established Vision One product score.

affected.product: Vision One server / Windows Runtime (dependency inclusion confirmed from release manifests)
affected.versions: 27.2.0, 27.2.1, 27.2.2 and the 27.2.3 release-preparation lockfile include node-forge 1.4.0. These are the reviewed baselines, not a complete affected-version range. Earlier releases and prereleases have not been comprehensively assessed in this notice and must not be assumed unaffected.
affected.action: Update to the published signed Vision One 27.2.4 installer or a later supported release under the site maintenance procedure. Retain certificate/CSR access protection and OT segmentation; do not replace individual packaged libraries.

impact: CVE-2026-85393 concerns acceptance of extra elements in the nested DigestAlgorithm sequence during node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification. Upstream reports that this can permit signature forgery with low-public-exponent RSA keys. The GitHub-reviewed upstream rating is High, CVSS 4.0 8.7 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N). This is an upstream base score, not a Vision One-specific exploitability assessment. No Vision One-specific CVSS score is assigned by this notice, and no authentication, license or TLS bypass is claimed to have been demonstrated.
assessment: Revision 2026-11-13: published signed 27.3.0-rc.2 passed Windows workflow 43415690895 and downloaded installer checksum/publisher signature verification, retaining node-forge 1.4.3 and the older RSA correction. This extends reviewed fixed prerelease scope, not the original affected-version range or a new RSA remediation. VO-SA-2026-004 remains separate; stable 27.2.5 is not patched for its additional Forge findings. Existing stable recommendations and bounded applicability limits remain.

Revision 2026-11-12: published signed 27.3.0-rc.1 retains node-forge 1.4.3 and this older RSA correction after successful Windows workflow 43232209650. It adds a reviewed fixed release candidate, not a new RSA remediation. VO-SA-2026-004 separately covers additional Forge findings, for which stable 27.2.5 is not a fixed baseline. Existing historical evidence and stable recommendations for this RSA CVE remain unchanged.

Revision 2026-11-11: published signed 27.3.0-beta.5 updates Server/PKI to node-forge 1.4.3, retaining this older RSA correction. The Windows gate and downloaded installer hash/publisher signature verification passed. Separate new certificate/Ed25519/TLS/HTTP findings are tracked in VO-SA-2026-004: earlier 1.4.2 releases are not fixes for those new issues. This RSA notice's stable remediation and older-version limitations remain unchanged.

Revision 2026-11-10: signed 27.3.0-beta.4 ships node-forge 1.4.2 and passed authoritative Windows Server/PKI production audits, PKI CLI, TLS transport, certificate metadata/alarm/preservation and HTTPS Chromium regressions in workflow 42787248122. The published installer hash and publisher signature were verified. The upstream RSA correction remains included; this is a qualified fixed prerelease, not complete stable 27.3 readiness or an exploit/penetration test. Stable update recommendations and older-version review limits remain.

Revision 2026-11-05: published stable 27.2.4 includes node-forge 1.4.2 in Server/PKI. The upstream 1.4.1 changelog explicitly identifies CVE-2026-85393 and requires canonical DER DigestInfo verification. Version 1.4.2 retains that correction and restores PEM Buffer compatibility. This notice is resolved for 27.2.4; older affected installations still require an update. The historical applicability evidence below does not assert successful remote exploitation.

Source discrepancy: the older GitHub-reviewed GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv record still lists no patched version when checked for this revision. The upstream 1.4.2 changelog and maintainer advisory GHSA-2g46-22mc-6gwp document the fix. Resolution is based on that upstream correction and the published 27.2.4 dependency baseline, not solely on npm audit output. Other forge parsing/certificate advisories were also addressed by the dependency update; this RSA-specific review is not an exhaustive applicability analysis of those separate issues.

Scope and evidence: the server release lockfiles at tags 27.2.0, 27.2.1 and 27.2.2 each list node-forge 1.4.0 as a production dependency. The reviewed application CSR and certificate-policy code is unchanged between those tags. This assessment is based on source and dependency-manifest review plus a benign library test, not an independent penetration test or extraction and examination of every published installer.

node-forge is actively used for local RSA key, certificate and CSR generation, CSR verification, certificate metadata parsing and ASN.1 algorithm inspection. Both newly generated CSRs and an existing CSR read from the local certificate directory can reach node-forge's RSA verification code. A benign RSA-3072 CSR round-trip confirmed that csr.verify() calls the RSA public-key verifier; this establishes code-path reachability, not successful exploitation.

Default application-generated RSA keys use 3072-bit moduli and public exponent 65537. This does not establish that every existing or externally provisioned key has the same exponent, nor does it make the affected library fixed. The reviewed CSR inputs are generated by the application or read from its local certificate directory. No unauthenticated remote endpoint accepting arbitrary CSR verification input was identified in the reviewed paths.

The reviewed server dependency metadata and a literal-import scan of the installed server dependencies did not identify an additional third-party consumer of node-forge. This is a bounded static review, not proof that every possible dynamic path or customer integration has been assessed.

The reviewed HTTPS and Project Replication transport paths use Node.js TLS/crypto, with certificate identity and fingerprint checks where configured; their use of node-forge for parsing or algorithm inspection does not by itself route TLS signature verification through the affected RSA verifier. License signatures use Node.js crypto with Ed25519 rather than this node-forge RSA path. These observations are limited to this CVE and are not a general security guarantee.

Historical conclusion on 2026-10-20: the vulnerable dependency was present and the affected verification function was reachable in local CSR handling; an exploitable remote Vision One path had not been established. The finding was open at that time. The 2026-11-05 revision supersedes that remediation status for published 27.2.4 without changing the original reachability limitations.
remediation: Update affected installations to the published signed Vision One 27.2.4 installer or a later supported release, with backups and installation-specific acceptance checks. This release ships patched node-forge 1.4.2; replacement of the PKI implementation is not required for this dependency fix and remains separate planned work. Existing invalid key/certificate material is preserved rather than silently replaced; certificate renewal can change fingerprints and requires normal trust/re-pairing review. Do not install unofficial forks or replace packaged library files.
workarounds: Restrict write access to the Vision One runtime data root and certificate/CSR directory to trusted, necessary operating-system accounts. Treat accounts able to modify private keys, CSRs, certificates or runtime files as security-sensitive.

Accept externally provisioned certificate/key/CSR material only through approved, trusted PKI and maintenance procedures. Do not substitute untrusted files or relax existing certificate and peer-fingerprint checks.

Restrict administrative access and keep runtime and replication endpoints within approved OT segments, VPNs or equivalent site controls. Network segmentation is defense in depth, not a demonstrated complete workaround for this library vulnerability.
These controls remain defense in depth and are not a substitute for the patched release. Request installation-specific guidance if certificate/CSR provenance or permissions are uncertain.
